Write cells as a SpatialData Zarr store

Source: R/store.R
writeCellStore.Rd

Writes a SpatialExperiment, SingleCellExperiment or data.frame of cells as a SpatialData Zarr store (Zarr v3), which spicy() reads a block of rows at a time, spatialdataR's readSpatialData() reads as a SpatialData object, and Python's spatialdata reads too. The cells become a table (AnnData, under tables/):

Usage

writeCellStore(
  cells,
  path,
  imageID = "imageID",
  spatialCoords = c("x", "y"),
  tableKey = "table",
  imageInfo = NULL,
  infoKey = "images",
  points = TRUE
)

Arguments

cells

A SpatialExperiment, SingleCellExperiment or data.frame with one row (column) per cell. The colData, rowData and data.frame columns are factors, character, integer, double or logical vectors, and every assay has a name.

path

The directory of the store (replaced if it exists).

imageID, spatialCoords

The column of the image and the two columns of the coordinates. A SpatialExperiment's own spatialCoords() are used unless spatialCoords names two colData columns.

tableKey

The name of the cell table.

imageInfo

Optional: a data.frame with one row per image, written as the table infoKey. The image IDs are its imageID column, or else its row names.

infoKey

The name of the per-image table.

points

Whether to write the cells as points too, one points element per image (needs duckdb).

Value

path, invisibly.

Details

  • obs: the colData (or the columns of a data.frame) other than the coordinates, factors as categorical columns. The image column is the table's region key (always categorical, its categories the levels of a factor, else the images in order of first appearance), and the cells are numbered 0, 1, ... in "instance_id".

  • X and layers: the first assay and the others (a sparse assay in compressed sparse row form).

  • var: the rowData, with the row names as its index.

  • obsm: the coordinates as "spatial", and the reducedDims.

The cells of each image also become a points element named after the image, with their coordinates and their "instance_id", so that the table annotates elements of the store (image IDs must then be valid element names: letters, digits, _, - and .). The images of a SpatialExperiment (imgData()) become image elements named <sample_id>_<image_id>, each in the coordinate system of its sample and scaled to the coordinates of the cells. A table with one row per image can be added. Every array is written in chunks (of 2^20 rows for a column) compressed with zstd, one chunk at a time, so writing needs little memory beyond that of cells, however many cells it has. metadata(), altExps() and column or row pairings are not written.

Examples

cells <- data.frame(imageID = factor(rep(c("a", "b"), each = 50)), cellType = factor(rep(c("T", "B"), 50)),
                    x = runif(100, 0, 100), y = runif(100, 0, 100))
if (requireNamespace("Rarr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  path <- writeCellStore(cells, tempfile(fileext = ".zarr"))
  list.files(file.path(path, "tables"))
}
#> [1] "table"     "zarr.json"
